title: Surface electromyography in canine spinal muscles
author: Ribeiro, Pereira, et al.

steps.title: Assemble and configure sEMG device
steps.instruction: Modify a ScientISSTⓇ device so that the onboard sEMG sensor has a pass‑band of 10 Hz to 400 Hz and a gain of 1000; connect three electrodes (positive differential lead, negative differential lead, and reference lead) and a 3‑axis accelerometer; set both sensors to be sampled at 1000 Hz; use the device’s 12‑bit ADC operating at 3.3 V, giving a measurable voltage range of 0 to 3.3 mV with an amplitude resolution of 0.81 µV; design a small enclosure for the sensor and fabricate it by 3‑D printing.

steps.title: Clip hair and clean electrode sites
steps.instruction: Clip the dog’s hair in three square areas of 1.5 cm × 1.5 cm: two sites over the paraspinal region between thoracic vertebra T12 (positive lead) and lumbar vertebra L2 (negative lead), spaced 1 cm apart, and one site on the medial aspect of the elbow for the reference lead; clean each area with alcohol to remove grease and lower skin impedance.

steps.title: Place electrodes and mount device
steps.instruction: Attach the positive, negative, and reference leads to the prepared sites described above; secure the sEMG sensor onto the animal’s torso using an adhesive retention bandage (10 cm × 10 m Omnifix E, Hartmann, South Africa) so that the three leads remain connected; allow the dog to become accustomed to the mounted device before starting signal acquisition.

steps.title: Execute movement protocol
steps.instruction: Perform each of the following activities for a duration that exceeds one minute:

substeps.instruction: Accelerating walk on a treadmill set to 0.7 mi/h (sub‑movement A).
Decelerating walk on the same treadmill (sub‑movement B).
Stable walking on the treadmill at 0.7 mi/h (sub‑movement C).
Balance on an oscillating wobble board (sub‑movement W).
Isometric position with front paws on a donut ball (sub‑movement D).
